page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It also bundles 1843 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and computational capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA extensions, resulting in a strong PassMark CPU encryption score. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached read/write operations fall within the average range. Ray tracing and image processing benchmarks also show strong performance, while software compilation and database operations perform at an average level.

The D48ads_v5 offers a balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring a mix of compute, memory, and local storage without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. A notable tradeoff is its performance on large-scale AI workloads; while text generation for small LLM models is strong, text generation for a large 70B model is poor, registering at 2.54 tokens per second. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded data processing, image processing, web serving, and applications requiring fast local temporary storage.
